description: Our project focuses on developing a Space Healthcare Monitoring System for astronauts. The aim is to monitor astronauts’ vital signs and health conditions during space missions, helping identify potential health risks and supporting timely medical intervention. We aim to explore innovative technology to make space missions safer and improve astronaut healthcare.
summary:
High level summary of our amazing project
ASTROCARE is a proposed Astronaut Health Monitoring and Decision-Support System designed to support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. Our project presents a unified dashboard concept that brings important health information together in one place.

The proposed system includes monitoring sections for vital signs such as heart rate, blood oxygen level (SpO2), body temperature and blood pressure. It also includes sleep and wellness tracking, radiation exposure records, health history and sample health alerts. Through a simple, user-friendly interface, astronauts and authorized medical teams can review health information and observe changes over time.

ASTROCARE addresses the challenge of organizing and monitoring astronaut health information in the demanding environment of space. Long-duration missions can expose astronauts to microgravity, radiation, sleep disturbances and physical stress. Having health-related information presented in one accessible dashboard could help support timely review and better-informed decisions.

Our goal is to contribute to safer and healthier human space exploration through an accessible and innovative digital solution. The current prototype is a conceptual mockup using simulated data, with future potential for integration with compatible health-monitoring sensors and validated NASA data sources.
details: ASTROCARE (Astronaut Health Monitoring and Decision-Support System) is a proposed digital health-monitoring solution designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It brings important health-related information together in a single, user-friendly dashboard. The proposed system includes modules for monitoring vital signs such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), body temperature and blood pressure. It also includes sleep and wellness tracking, radiation exposure records, health history and health-status alerts. The dashboard is designed to display health information, visualize changes over time and highlight readings that may require further review. ASTROCARE aims to make astronaut health information easier to access, understand and review. By organizing multiple health indicators in one place, it could help astronauts and authorized medical teams observe changes in health measurements and maintain a clearer record of health-related information. The project focuses on contributing to safer and healthier human space exploration. Long-duration space missions can expose astronauts to microgravity, radiation, sleep disturbances and physical stress. ASTROCARE addresses these challenges through an integrated dashboard concept that brings different aspects of astronaut health monitoring together. Our project is creative because it combines vital signs, sleep, wellness and radiation records into one space-oriented interface rather than presenting them as separate systems. Its visual design and health-history features aim to make complex information easier to understand. Our team uses ChatGPT for brainstorming, research organization and project documentation. The prototype is being developed as a visual mockup, with the aim of exploring future integration with compatible health-monitoring sensors and validated NASA data resources. During development, we considered usability, data accuracy, privacy, reliability and the limitations of a beginner-level prototype. The current concept uses simulated data and is not a clinically validated medical device. It is intended to demonstrate a potential digital solution for supporting astronaut health monitoring, not to replace professional medical judgement.
